title: Western North Pacific 26.5 outcrop-region freshening of 1990-2017 reached 400 m on sigma0 25.6-26.7 with cooling, not by mixing or local E-P (WOD ship and Argo casts, 1950-2025)
abstract: Question: the late-winter surface of the western North Pacific outcrop region of sigma0 26.5 (box W, 36-48 N, 145 E-180) became fresher in 1990-2017, and local Ekman transport and local E-P do not explain it. Is the freshening a vertical redistribution of salt, a mixed-layer freshwater gain, or a deep-reaching water-mass change? Approach: 346,092 World Ocean Database casts (ship and Argo, 30-60 N, 140 E-170 W) gave T and S at 5-800 m and on sigma0 25.6-27.0; epoch changes against 1965-1984 used cell-month fixed effects and a cruise bootstrap under a plan with decision rules fixed before analysis. Results: in 2006-2017 W was 0.108 psu fresher at 0-30 m (95% 0.087-0.134), 0.085 at 150 m and 0.048 at 400 m. The 0-400 m freshwater gain was 0.66-1.01 m in 1990-2017, 3.6-5.5 times the mixed-layer anomaly. The 150-400 m layer became fresher, not saltier, and ship mixed layers did not shoal, so redistribution is rejected. Salinity fell by 0.07-0.09 psu on 25.6-26.6, already in 1990-2000, about 0.03 on 26.7 and not on 26.8-27.0; the pre-set water-mass rule passed in 2001-2005 and 2006-2017. The thermocline also cooled (150 m: -0.37 to -0.70 deg C in 1990-2005), which marks subarctic-type water. Local NCEP E-P can store 0.04-0.33 m with 2-10 yr flushing. Surface S enters 26.6-26.7 in the same year (r 0.51-0.59, p <= 0.004) but not 26.8. In 2018-2025 the surface recovered, but 0.24 m of freshwater stayed at 150-400 m. The subarctic box did not freshen on these classes (+0.03 to +0.08 psu); the Kuroshio-side thermocline freshened later, step by step to -0.107 psu on 26.5. Exploratory: a two-end-member mix fitted with T predicts annual W surface S (r 0.81) and assigns the W lightening to warming of both source waters (0.04-0.15 kg/m3), while a 3-6 point larger subarctic share made W denser; this is weak where 26.5 outcrops. Limitations: ships are 0.13 psu fresher and 0.74 deg C colder than Argo in the same cells (density-compensated), so mixed-layer depth changes are not usable and the 2018-2025 surface recovery is Argo-based; no geostrophic or eddy flux terms; the mixing split is post hoc.

Salinity change on density surfaces in four boxes for 2006-2017 and 2018-2025. W and the Kuroshio side freshened; the subarctic box became saltier.

(a) Box W freshwater gain: mixed layer only, 0-100, 0-200 and 0-400 m, and local NCEP E-P storage. (b) Exploratory two-end-member split of the W surface density change; bars give the mean and range over five end-member box sets.

citations.reason: We adapt its WOD reader and box W. It named entrainment and lateral terms as the likely source of the off-line freshening; we reject entrainment-driven redistribution and find a deep-reaching water-mass change with cooling.
We use its reference epoch and question one detail: in the same cells ships are 0.13 psu fresher than Argo in W (density-compensated), which affects T-S partitions of the surface change.
Its 1990-2000 freshening episode appears in our data as a 0.07-0.09 psu salinity drop on sigma0 25.6-26.6 down to about 250 m.
The outcrop-region change that it links to the oxygen loss is a change on the same ventilated classes (25.6-26.7) in our analysis.

It attributed half of the outcrop lightening to freshening; our exploratory two-end-member split assigns the lightening to warming of both source waters, with the extra subarctic water making W fresher but denser.
Its isopycnal freshening west of 150 W agrees with our 0.07-0.09 psu freshening on sigma0 25.6-26.6 in box W.
Within-type O2 loss on the classes that stopped outcropping; our salinity change is on the same classes.
Context: the outcrop mechanism is a North Pacific threshold effect.
Oka et al. (2017) reported subtropical thermocline freshening since the mid-1990s from the Kuroshio Extension winter mixed layer; our KUR box freshened after box W, in steps to 2025.
WOD23 geographic files (OSD, CTD, PFL); exact files and hashes in files/provenance.
